logicalBugs.description: Twenty’s Kanban board view arranges record cards in columns, often grouped by status or a linked record. Moving a Task or Opportunity (sales deal) card between columns saves its new status or stage but changes the destination column to manual-position ordering. The selected sort, such as Title or Amount, still appears active while cards no longer follow it; reloading the board restores the displayed order.
logicalBugs.rootCause: A sorted cross-column board move updates the grouping field without a new position. Both the optimistic destination insertion and the subsequent reposition path order by position rather than the active record sorts, leaving moved cards out of their displayed sort order until refetch.
reproductionPaths: Twenty’s Kanban board view arranges record cards in columns, often grouped by status or a linked record. Changing an opportunity’s Kanban stage replaces the destination column’s active sort with manual-position ordering until the board is reloaded.

Twenty’s Kanban board view arranges record cards in columns, often grouped by status or a linked record. A cross-column Task drag changes Status correctly but reorders the destination using manual position, contradicting the still-active saved Title sort.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty can narrow a record list with field filters and a Search any field query. Search inside a linked-record filter can find a person by either part of their name but not their full displayed name. This affects Opportunity (sales deal) Point of Contact and Company Account Owner selection; the matching person exists and individual-name searches find them.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The relation-filter picker uses useRecordsForSelect, which searches the entire query independently in name.firstName and name.lastName. A full displayed name cannot match either component by itself.
reproductionPaths: Twenty can narrow a record list with field filters and a Search any field query. Point of Contact filter search fails for an existing contact’s full displayed name, while either individual name part finds the same contact.

Twenty can narrow a record list with field filters and a Search any field query. The Companies Account Owner filter finds a workspace member by either name part but returns No results for the same member’s full displayed name.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty saved views display records in a chosen layout and retain their configured settings. Removing a saved sort and adding the same field back makes Update view fail. The replacement sort does not save, while other changes can partially persist.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The Sort menu replaces the saved sort ID with a fresh client ID. useSaveRecordSortsToViewSorts classifies it as a create plus destroy and performs creation first; the existing saved field sort still occupies its unique key, so the create fails before deletion.
reproductionPaths: Twenty saved views display records in a chosen layout and retain their configured settings. Removing a saved sort and adding the same field back makes Update view fail. The replacement sort does not save, while other changes can partially persist.

Twenty saved views display records in a chosen layout and retain their configured settings. Keep an existing saved sort chip, reopen Sort and choose that same field again. Update view fails with a migration error and the replacement sort does not persist; changing direction through the existing chip works.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty’s Calendar view places records on dates using a chosen date field. Switching a grouped Table or board to Calendar can leave the calendar configured with one date field while its records use another. Records may disappear despite existing in the displayed period, or Task cards may use a different date from the Due Date shown in the selector. This concerns layout transitions rather than changing a record’s saved date.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Calendar entry first loads new date/calendar state, then updateCurrentView handles the grouping reset by calling loadRecordIndexStates with its captured pre-update currentView. That second full-state load restores old calendar metadata and grouping, so the calendar query has an invalid/stale configuration until reload.
reproductionPaths: Twenty’s Calendar view places records on dates using a chosen date field. Changing a grouped Table or Kanban (a board of cards in columns) view to Calendar produces a blank calendar even though Creation date is selected and records exist in the displayed month.

Twenty’s Calendar view places records on dates using a chosen date field. Start with a saved Tasks Calendar using Due Date, switch through Kanban (a board of cards in columns) and return to Calendar. The selector still shows Due Date while cards are placed using a different date field.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty can narrow a record list with field filters and a Search any field query. Changing which field an already-saved filter uses does not reliably replace the old field. New values can be saved under the previous field, producing incorrect labels or empty results after reload, or a valid rule for the new type can fail validation against the old field.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The existing view-filter update payload includes value, operand and target/subfield changes but omits fieldMetadataId. Changing the source field is detected as an edit yet persists the new values against the old field.
reproductionPaths: Twenty can narrow a record list with field filters and a Search any field query. Changing an existing saved filter from Amount to Stage saves the Stage values but retains the old Amount field. Reloading displays raw Stage values under Amount and returns no matching records.

Twenty can narrow a record list with field filters and a Search any field query. Change the field used by an existing saved advanced-filter rule to a field of another type, then save. Validation still treats the rule as belonging to the old field, so the newly valid condition is rejected.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty can divide table rows or board cards into groups based on a field value. Record-list header counts and grouped Table calculations can disagree with the rows that are displayed. Combining search, field filters or group conditions can leave summaries counting excluded records; in a Workflow Runs (execution history) table, linked-record grouping can instead show matching rows with a zero total. These cases concern incorrect summaries, not missing saved records.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Table footer and header aggregate hooks combine independently compiled filters using object spread. Group, explicit filters and any-field search can each contain top-level and/or keys; later objects replace earlier predicates rather than conjoining them, so summaries include records excluded by the row query.
reproductionPaths: Twenty can divide table rows or board cards into groups based on a field value. Filtering a Stage-grouped Opportunities (sales deals) table to one stage removes the other stages’ rows, but their empty groups still show Amount averages and other calculations from excluded records.

Twenty can divide table rows or board cards into groups based on a field value. Combining Search any field with advanced OR rules displays the correct matching records but reports a larger total that ignores the advanced rules.

Twenty can divide table rows or board cards into groups based on a field value. A single basic People Name filter combined with Search any field filters the visible rows correctly but leaves the total count and footer calculations describing the larger search-only result set.

Twenty can divide table rows or board cards into groups based on a field value. A basic empty-Amount filter and any-field search correctly restrict Opportunity (sales deal) rows, while header and table summary calculations ignore the Amount condition.

Twenty can divide table rows or board cards into groups based on a field value. Company Is not correctly excludes People rows, but the view count and column-footer summary calculations discard that exclusion when Search any field is active.

Twenty can divide table rows or board cards into groups based on a field value. Use Search any field on Companies and add a Name Is empty filter that excludes all matching rows. The list becomes empty but its header still reports matching records; Is not empty and other controls work.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty can divide table rows or board cards into groups based on a field value. Alphabetical and Reverse Alphabetical group ordering works immediately in grouped Table and Kanban (a board of cards in columns) views but resets to Manual after reload, including Opportunity (sales deal) Stage, Task Status and Workflow Runs (execution history) views.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The group-order menu updates an in-memory component state defaulting to Manual. Column ordering reads it, but view persistence and loading omit that setting. Neighboring visibility settings use stored view fields.
reproductionPaths: Twenty can divide table rows or board cards into groups based on a field value. Alphabetical or Reverse Alphabetical Stage ordering applies in an Opportunities (sales deals) Kanban (a board of cards in columns) view but resets to Manual after full reload.

Twenty can divide table rows or board cards into groups based on a field value. Alphabetical and Reverse Alphabetical Stage group ordering in saved Opportunities (sales deals) Table views resets to Manual on full reload.

Twenty can divide table rows or board cards into groups based on a field value. Alphabetical or Reverse Alphabetical Status group ordering in a Tasks Kanban (a board of cards in columns) view resets to Manual on full reload.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty can narrow a record list with field filters and a Search any field query. Multi-word full-name filtering matches any entered word instead of requiring every word, causing overinclusion and overexclusion.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Helper flattens token×name-component clauses; Contains ORs all clauses, negative operator ANDs each separate negation. Corrected helper ANDs per-token OR groups.
reproductionPaths: Twenty can narrow a record list with field filters and a Search any field query. Multi-word full-name filtering matches any entered word instead of requiring every word, causing overinclusion and overexclusion.

Twenty can narrow a record list with field filters and a Search any field query. Enter a multi-word full name in People’s Search any field query. Results match either word separately rather than the complete search, including people who do not match the full name.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty saved views display records in a chosen layout and retain their configured settings. When a saved view sorts on a field containing empty values, record-page Next/Previous navigation can omit those empty-valued records and show a total that is too small. Accepted cases include Tasks without Due Date and Companies without Annual Revenue. The records still exist in the originating list.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Client before/after filters use date gt/lt without a NULL alternative, excluding undated tasks despite DescNullsLast ordering. Summed neighbor counts understate total and wrap navigation prematurely. The server applies these explicit filters and ordinary SQL date comparisons.
reproductionPaths: Twenty saved views display records in a chosen layout and retain their configured settings. Record-page navigation skips undated Tasks and reports incorrect totals when the parent view sorts by Due Date.

Twenty saved views display records in a chosen layout and retain their configured settings. Open Company records from a view sorted by Annual Revenue descending, including a Company with no revenue value. The record-page total is too small and Next wraps around without visiting the empty-revenue record.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty can narrow a record list with field filters and a Search any field query. Ungrouped Search any field results do not reconcile record edits or creation: an edited Person can remain after it stops matching, and a newly created matching Person can be absent, although the aggregate count updates.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The virtualized table checks explicit field filters, sorts and position when deciding whether an update requires resetting its row list. It omits the separate any-field search value. The count can update while the existing virtualized row remains; resetting would refetch with the search applied.
reproductionPaths: Twenty can narrow a record list with field filters and a Search any field query. An existing Person edited out of an ungrouped any-field search remains visible while the count correctly becomes zero.

Twenty can narrow a record list with field filters and a Search any field query. Creating and naming a Person to match an Any field search increases the header count but leaves the new row absent after closing its panel. Reload reveals the saved record; basic Name-filter and unfiltered controls insert it immediately.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty’s Kanban board view arranges record cards in columns, often grouped by status or a linked record. With Hide empty groups enabled, moving a Task or Opportunity (sales deal) into an initially empty configured status/stage group can leave that destination hidden. The change saves but its card disappears from the board until refresh or a visibility change. The failure is a now-populated group staying hidden, not automatic creation of unconfigured groups.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Initial board loading synchronizes both record IDs and a separate empty-group flag. Drop and reposition paths update group memberships without synchronizing that flag. Column body and header visibility still consult the stale empty flag, hiding a now-populated destination. This causal chain is inferred from source and observed controls rather than direct atom instrumentation.
reproductionPaths: Twenty’s Kanban board view arranges record cards in columns, often grouped by status or a linked record. A Task moved into an initially empty Status column disappears when Hide empty groups is enabled, despite its saved status and nonempty destination.

Twenty’s Kanban board view arranges record cards in columns, often grouped by status or a linked record. With Hide empty enabled, dragging an Opportunity (sales deal) into an initially empty configured Stage can leave the now-populated destination hidden. The count remains populated; reload exposes the saved card. In the tested filtered view, moving all displayed cards can leave a blank board.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty saved views display records in a chosen layout and retain their configured settings. Changing a saved view’s layout, Group by field or column calculation can replace its currently applied but unsaved filters and sorts with the saved settings. The displayed record set changes even though the user changed presentation rather than asking to reset filtering. This includes Table/board transitions and Workflow Runs (execution history) grouping.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Changing layout/grouping calls useUpdateCurrentView, which reloads all index states from the previously saved currentView when grouping changes. The saved filters overwrite the active unsaved filters even though this action only changes presentation.
reproductionPaths: Twenty saved views display records in a chosen layout and retain their configured settings. Changing the layout of the current saved view silently replaces its applied but unsaved filters and sorts with saved settings.

Twenty saved views display records in a chosen layout and retain their configured settings. Apply a Title filter to the Tasks By Status board, then change a column calculation such as Count all or Count empty. The filter is discarded and previously excluded Tasks reappear.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty’s Kanban board view arranges record cards in columns, often grouped by status or a linked record. Moving a task between Kanban status columns removes its visible related-person chip until the record is reloaded, while the record link remains saved.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Board updates write partial mutation records and relation optimistic results back into the shared record store. The Task card Relations field depends on expanded target connections that are not included in the status-only mutation response; replacing that connection loses the rendered chip until the board/detail query refetches it.
reproductionPaths: Twenty’s Kanban board view arranges record cards in columns, often grouped by status or a linked record. Moving a task between Kanban status columns removes its visible related-person chip until the record is reloaded, while the record link remains saved.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty saved views display records in a chosen layout and retain their configured settings. Creating a saved view with an empty or whitespace-only name produces a persistent unlabeled entry in the view selector.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The view picker passes its raw name to createViewFromCurrentView, whose name fallback uses nullish coalescing. An empty string is therefore a supplied name rather than a missing value and reaches view creation without a nonempty-name guard.
reproductionPaths: Twenty saved views display records in a chosen layout and retain their configured settings. Creating a saved view with an empty or whitespace-only name produces a persistent unlabeled entry in the view selector.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty’s Calendar view places records on dates using a chosen date field. Calendar cards stay in their existing position order when the selected record sort changes, even after saving and reloading the view.
logicalBugs.rootCause: useRecordCalendarGroupByRecords builds orderByForRecords solely from position ascending. It never reads currentRecordSorts, so changing the saved sort does not change the calendar query ordering.
reproductionPaths: Twenty’s Calendar view places records on dates using a chosen date field. Calendar cards stay in their existing position order when the selected record sort changes, even after saving and reloading the view.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty can divide table rows or board cards into groups based on a field value. Grouping a Table view with only one eligible grouping field disables Group by, making the None option inaccessible.
logicalBugs.rootCause: ObjectOptionsDropdownRecordGroupsContent disables the Group by menu when hasOnlyOneGroupByOption is true, even for an already grouped Table that needs the None reset choice. The disable guard prevents reaching that reset.
reproductionPaths: Twenty can divide table rows or board cards into groups based on a field value. Grouping a Table view with only one eligible grouping field disables Group by, making the None option inaccessible.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty saved views display records in a chosen layout and retain their configured settings. Shift-clicking a table row range leaves the clicked endpoint visibly checked but excludes it from the selected count and bulk-action targets.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Row checkbox clicks are handled by the wrapping div while the inner Checkbox maintains its own checked state. Shift range selection toggles the current row from shared selection state while the inner primitive also handles the click; their separate updates can leave the endpoint visibly checked without its row-selection atom participating in the bulk selection. Source-informed hypothesis: the cited implementation contains the relevant failure boundary, but the exact triggering event order was not independently reproduced during this clustering pass.
reproductionPaths: Twenty saved views display records in a chosen layout and retain their configured settings. Shift-clicking a table row range leaves the clicked endpoint visibly checked but excludes it from the selected count and bulk-action targets.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty’s Company Domain Name field stores a URL and an optional display label. A negative filter such as Doesn’t contain .com wrongly excludes a non-.com domain when its optional label is empty, even though that URL satisfies the filter. A populated label can avoid the exclusion; positive Contains filtering works.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The LINKS Does not contain converter combines negative ILIKE checks across composite link fields without admitting null primary labels. SQL NOT of a comparison with NULL remains unknown, so a company with an unset label is excluded even when its URL does not contain the query.
reproductionPaths: Twenty’s Company Domain Name field stores a URL and an optional display label. A negative filter such as Doesn’t contain .com wrongly excludes a non-.com domain when its optional label is empty, even though that URL satisfies the filter. A populated label can avoid the exclusion; positive Contains filtering works.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty can narrow a record list with field filters and a Search any field query. Record-page Next/Previous omits the originating list’s Search any field query and navigates to records outside the matching results.
logicalBugs.rootCause: useQueryVariablesFromParentView reconstructs navigation filters from parentViewFilters and parentViewFilterGroups but does not include the separate anyFieldFilterValue. Neighbor and count queries therefore navigate the full saved/explicit-filter view rather than the searched subset.
reproductionPaths: Twenty can narrow a record list with field filters and a Search any field query. Record-page Next/Previous omits the originating list’s Search any field query and navigates to records outside the matching results.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty can narrow a record list with field filters and a Search any field query. Search any field does not find saved text in a Task or Note Body, while matching title text is searchable.
logicalBugs.rootCause: turnAnyFieldFilterIntoRecordGqlFilter handles selected scalar/composite metadata types but has no RICH_TEXT branch. Task/Note bodyV2 BlockNote content consequently contributes no predicate to Search any field.
reproductionPaths: Twenty can narrow a record list with field filters and a Search any field query. Search any field does not find saved text in a Task or Note Body, while matching title text is searchable.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty saved views display records in a chosen layout and retain their configured settings. Saving multiple new sorts together can change their priority after reload, changing the view’s record order even though sort directions are retained.
logicalBugs.rootCause: View sort persistence stores field/direction/subfield but no priority position; loading maps viewSorts in returned metadata order without restoring the active sort sequence. Multiple sort precedence can therefore change after metadata reload.
reproductionPaths: Twenty saved views display records in a chosen layout and retain their configured settings. Saving multiple new sorts together can change their priority after reload, changing the view’s record order even though sort directions are retained.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty’s Kanban board view arranges record cards in columns, often grouped by status or a linked record. Moving an opportunity in an Amount-filtered Kanban can throw an amountMicros error before saving when the record was previously loaded without its Amount field. The card appears to move, but totals stay stale and reload restores its old stage.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Optimistic list-filter evaluation passes record[filterKey] into isMatchingCurrencyFilter without ensuring a currency value was fetched. A partially cached Opportunity lacks Amount, and the matcher dereferences amountMicros before the stage mutation can complete.
reproductionPaths: Twenty’s Kanban board view arranges record cards in columns, often grouped by status or a linked record. Moving an opportunity in an Amount-filtered Kanban can throw an amountMicros error before saving when the record was previously loaded without its Amount field. The card appears to move, but totals stay stale and reload restores its old stage.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty saved views display records in a chosen layout and retain their configured settings. Returning with browser Back from a full record page loses the browsing position in a long ungrouped table, while the record-page breadcrumb (page navigation link) returns near the opened row.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The virtualized table remount calls triggerInitialRecordTableDataLoad with its default scroll-to-start behavior. The previously loaded row/scroll state is reset rather than restored for browser Back navigation.
reproductionPaths: Twenty saved views display records in a chosen layout and retain their configured settings. Returning with browser Back from a full record page loses the browsing position in a long ungrouped table, while the record-page breadcrumb (page navigation link) returns near the opened row.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty saved views display records in a chosen layout and retain their configured settings. Closing the Options menu within about 500 milliseconds of editing a saved view name discards the pending rename. Pressing Enter before closing does not commit it.
logicalBugs.rootCause: ObjectOptionsDropdownMenuViewName debounces persistence for 500ms and does not flush on unmount. Closing Options before that callback runs discards the pending rename.
reproductionPaths: Twenty saved views display records in a chosen layout and retain their configured settings. Closing the Options menu within about 500 milliseconds of editing a saved view name discards the pending rename. Pressing Enter before closing does not commit it.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty saved views display records in a chosen layout and retain their configured settings. Creating a new People view from current settings drops the selected Name sort subfield, replacing Last name sorting with First name and changing the persisted row order.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Copying view sorts maps and retains subFieldName locally, but createViewSortInputs in useCreateViewFromCurrentView sends only ID, fieldMetadataId, viewId and direction. The saved Name sort loses lastName and resolves to the default firstName subfield.
reproductionPaths: Twenty saved views display records in a chosen layout and retain their configured settings. Creating a new People view from current settings drops the selected Name sort subfield, replacing Last name sorting with First name and changing the persisted row order.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty’s Calendar view places records on dates using a chosen date field. Task Calendar views silently cap cards shown on a busy date: Month shows five and Week/Day show ten, with no overflow or loading control. Filtering for an omitted Task makes it appear.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The calendar groupBy query returns only the server-default first page of records in each due-date group. useRecordCalendarGroupByRecords flattens those connections without fetching their next pages or exposing a load-more mechanism; Month further limits visible cards per day.
reproductionPaths: Twenty’s Calendar view places records on dates using a chosen date field. Use a Task Calendar with more matching Tasks on one date than its display cap. Month shows only five cards and Week or Day only ten, with no way to reveal the rest; filtering for an omitted Task makes it appear.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty’s Kanban board view arranges record cards in columns, often grouped by status or a linked record. The built-in By Status board excludes tasks assigned the selectable No Status value, with no uncategorized group available. They remain in All Tasks and in a newly created Kanban view's No Value group.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The standard Tasks By Status view defines groups only for its enumerated status options. Its saved group definitions omit the nullable empty-status group that generic new-view creation adds, so No Status records have no visible board column.
reproductionPaths: Twenty’s Kanban board view arranges record cards in columns, often grouped by status or a linked record. The built-in By Status board excludes tasks assigned the selectable No Status value, with no uncategorized group available. They remain in All Tasks and in a newly created Kanban view's No Value group.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty saved views display records in a chosen layout and retain their configured settings. The Companies table cannot retain two selected owned rows: selecting the second replaces the first. The precise reported post-click state differed—the second row was checked and the count stayed at one—but multi-selection still failed.
logicalBugs.rootCause: RecordTable starts drag selection by unconditionally resetting the existing row-selection state. The checkbox/drag-select event boundary can enter that start path while selecting another row, replacing the earlier selection rather than accumulating it. This is the source-supported event path; the precise event ordering in the supplied Tim Apple reproduction is inferred. Source-informed hypothesis: the cited implementation contains the relevant failure boundary, but the exact triggering event order was not independently reproduced during this clustering pass.
reproductionPaths: Twenty saved views display records in a chosen layout and retain their configured settings. Select one Company row and then a second row using their checkboxes. The table fails to retain both selections and its selected count stays at one; the recorded post-click checkbox details varied.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty saved views display records in a chosen layout and retain their configured settings. The List Members journey reports a nonzero count but renders no table, column headers or record rows. Options opens an empty menu and Create View cannot configure a usable view.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The standard view metadata builder registers a view for messageList but no messageListMember view. The generic List Members index has records/count but no current view ID or view fields, so rendering and Create View initialization cannot obtain their required view context.
reproductionPaths: Twenty saved views display records in a chosen layout and retain their configured settings. Open the List Members record list, which represents members of mailing lists. A nonzero record count appears, but there are no column headers or rows; Options is empty and creating a view cannot make the list usable.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty can narrow a record list with field filters and a Search any field query. Searching a Task or Note in linked-record filter pickers returns an invalid-filter error and no results, preventing selection of existing matching records.
logicalBugs.rootCause: getObjectFilterFields special-cases only Person and WorkspaceMember names and returns name for all other objects. Task and Note use title as their identifier, so relation-picker search constructs a filter on a nonexistent name field.
reproductionPaths: Twenty can narrow a record list with field filters and a Search any field query. Search for an existing Task or Note in a picker used to filter by a linked record. The picker returns an invalid-filter error and no matching results, preventing selection.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty saved views display records in a chosen layout and retain their configured settings. Selected table rows become unchecked when a different saved view is renamed in another tab, despite leaving the selected table untouched.
logicalBugs.rootCause: View metadata updates can re-run index state initialization and selection resets through shared metadata synchronization, even when the changed view belongs to a different object. The selection lifetime is coupled to view-store reload rather than solely the active table/query identity; the exact asynchronous reset sequence is inferred from the reported cross-tab transition. Source-informed hypothesis: the cited implementation contains the relevant failure boundary, but the exact triggering event order was not independently reproduced during this clustering pass.
reproductionPaths: Twenty saved views display records in a chosen layout and retain their configured settings. Selected table rows become unchecked when a different saved view is renamed in another tab, despite leaving the selected table untouched.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty can narrow a record list with field filters and a Search any field query. After searching for an Account Owner value, the same search text remains in the advanced-filter field picker and hides unrelated field choices.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Advanced-filter field search and value search reuse objectFilterDropdownSearchInputComponentState. Switching from a searched value picker to the field picker retains the same string instead of clearing or separately scoping it, hiding unrelated field choices.
reproductionPaths: Twenty can narrow a record list with field filters and a Search any field query. After searching for an Account Owner value, the same search text remains in the advanced-filter field picker and hides unrelated field choices.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty can narrow a record list with field filters and a Search any field query. Filtering People by a full displayed phone number with its country code omits the matching person, while searching the national-number portion finds that same record.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The PHONES Contains converter strips formatting then compares the entire digit string independently against primaryPhoneNumber and primaryPhoneCallingCode. It never concatenates calling code with the national number, so a complete displayed international number does not match either stored component.
reproductionPaths: Twenty can narrow a record list with field filters and a Search any field query. Filtering People by a full displayed phone number with its country code omits the matching person, while searching the national-number portion finds that same record.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty’s Kanban board view arranges record cards in columns, often grouped by status or a linked record. On a Kanban loaded with Amount hidden, showing Amount renders empty placeholders instead of the saved amounts until the board is refreshed.
logicalBugs.rootCause: RecordBoardQueryEffect keys its refetch on filter/order/query and group IDs, without tracking visible field changes. Revealing a field changes the requested projection but does not reload existing board records, so cards retain missing values until another refetch.
reproductionPaths: Twenty’s Kanban board view arranges record cards in columns, often grouped by status or a linked record. On a Kanban loaded with Amount hidden, showing Amount renders empty placeholders instead of the saved amounts until the board is refreshed.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty’s Kanban board view arranges record cards in columns, often grouped by status or a linked record. The same saved descending Name sort orders lowercase and uppercase names differently in Table and Kanban layouts.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The board optimistic cache sorter uses JavaScript string comparison while table data is ordered by the server database collation. Their case ordering differs, so the same saved Name sort yields different Table and Kanban orderings.
reproductionPaths: Twenty’s Kanban board view arranges record cards in columns, often grouped by status or a linked record. The same saved descending Name sort orders lowercase and uppercase names differently in Table and Kanban layouts.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty’s Kanban board view arranges record cards in columns, often grouped by status or a linked record. In an unsorted Kanban column, an upward keyboard drop announces the previous card as its target but does not reorder the card. Downward keyboard drops work and persist.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Board drag-end resolves insertion using pointer Y and adjusts destination indexes for removal of the dragged source. Keyboard ArrowUp supplies a target position through the same pointer resolver; the upward index adjustment can resolve back to sourceIndex and trigger the no-op guard.
reproductionPaths: Twenty’s Kanban board view arranges record cards in columns, often grouped by status or a linked record. In an unsorted Kanban column, an upward keyboard drop announces the previous card as its target but does not reorder the card. Downward keyboard drops work and persist.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty saved views display records in a chosen layout and retain their configured settings. An immediate reload after an acknowledged sort save can initialize stale unsorted state; clicking the offered Update view then permanently removes the retained saved sort.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The client can initialize active sorts once from stale cached view metadata. Later fresh saved sorts do not reinitialize that active list, and Update view interprets missing active sorts as intentional deletions.
reproductionPaths: Twenty saved views display records in a chosen layout and retain their configured settings. An immediate reload after an acknowledged sort save can initialize stale unsorted state; clicking the offered Update view then permanently removes the retained saved sort.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty can narrow a record list with field filters and a Search any field query. Ordinary UI Contains and Does not contain filters interpret typed percent and underscore as SQL wildcard syntax, including records without the typed punctuation or excluding them incorrectly.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The shared UI filter converter interpolates raw text into percent-wrapped ILIKE patterns, including composite-name tokens, without escaping user-entered percent or underscore. The server correctly evaluates those supplied patterns.
reproductionPaths: Twenty can narrow a record list with field filters and a Search any field query. Enter a literal percent sign or underscore in a Contains or Does not contain text filter. The characters act as wildcard patterns instead of required punctuation, so unrelated records are included or matching records are excluded.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty can divide table rows or board cards into groups based on a field value. Removing table grouping persists successfully but leaves the previous operational grouping and field selection active until reload.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The reset persists null grouping metadata without reloading record-index/group state. Rendering retains old group IDs and the same-view initialization does not reset them.
reproductionPaths: Twenty can divide table rows or board cards into groups based on a field value. Remove grouping from a Table view and let the change save. Rows and the field selector continue using the previous grouping until reload, even though grouping was successfully removed from the saved view.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty saved views display records in a chosen layout and retain their configured settings. Returning through a record breadcrumb (page navigation link) to an index without viewId displays the saved view, but reload selects the default and replaces the remembered view ID.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The no-viewId initialization and persisted last-visited-view synchronization can select a fallback and write it over the remembered saved-view ID. Storage replacement is directly observed; exact hydration, subscription and effect ordering is inferred from source.
reproductionPaths: Twenty saved views display records in a chosen layout and retain their configured settings. Return from a record page using its breadcrumb (page navigation link) link to a list URL without an explicit view identifier. The expected saved view initially appears, but reloading selects the default view instead.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty can narrow a record list with field filters and a Search any field query. Creating a Company through the top New action in a populated filtered group can leave a stale unselectable row after the committed name no longer matches the filter.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Query synchronization first inserts the created record into group IDs, then createNewIndexRecord independently prepends the same ID. Duplicate React keys support the residual-DOM explanation; exact reconciliation ordering was not instrumented.
reproductionPaths: Twenty can narrow a record list with field filters and a Search any field query. Creating a Company through the top New action in a populated filtered group can leave a stale unselectable row after the committed name no longer matches the filter.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty’s Calendar view places records on dates using a chosen date field. Returning a saved view to Calendar replaces its retained date-field, layout and end-field choices with defaults.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Calendar entry unconditionally chooses availableFieldsForCalendar[0], Month, null end; frontend persists replacement values to same saved view. Table does not clear saved calendar settings.
reproductionPaths: Twenty’s Calendar view places records on dates using a chosen date field. Returning a saved view to Calendar replaces its retained date-field, layout and end-field choices with defaults.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty can narrow a record list with field filters and a Search any field query. Search any field omits People whose matching company name is shown in their Company field, while own text-field search and the dedicated Company filter work.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The Any field filter converter visits the current object’s metadata and generates predicates only for its supported scalar/composite field types. RELATION has no case, so it generates no condition for Company. The dedicated Company filter uses a separate supported relation-filter path.
reproductionPaths: Twenty can narrow a record list with field filters and a Search any field query. Search any field omits People whose matching company name is shown in their Company field, while own text-field search and the dedicated Company filter work.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty can narrow a record list with field filters and a Search any field query. On a People view with an advanced Company → Name text condition, New Person and Add New fail with an error instead of creating a record and opening its drawer.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Creation-default conversion treats a relation-traversal text value as the source relation foreign key. Separately, the optimistic list matcher treats a nested relation filter as a UUID filter. Depending on the cached-query/filter shape, creation aborts in that client matcher or reaches server UUID validation with the wrong Company ID.
reproductionPaths: Twenty can narrow a record list with field filters and a Search any field query. On a People view with an advanced Company → Name text condition, New Person and Add New fail with an error instead of creating a record and opening its drawer.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty can divide table rows or board cards into groups based on a field value. Activating a grouped Table row drag renders its preview without the required body context and crashes the table page.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Grouped table bodies put their per-group RecordTableBodyContext providers inside the outer drag provider. The drag overlay is rendered alongside those children, outside their contexts, but renders real table cells that require the context. The required-context hook throws. Ungrouped tables wrap the drag provider with the needed context.
reproductionPaths: Twenty can divide table rows or board cards into groups based on a field value. Start dragging a row in a grouped Table view. Displaying the drag preview crashes the page instead of allowing the row to be moved.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty’s Calendar view places records on dates using a chosen date field. A calendar query excludes a late Task starting before the grid even though its intended one-hour fallback duration overlaps the first displayed day.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The display selector gives records without an end a one-hour interval. With no compatible end field, the calendar query instead filters start times to the displayed month grid without allowing that fallback interval to overlap its leading boundary. A preceding-day Task is never fetched for the selector to place on the first day.
reproductionPaths: Twenty’s Calendar view places records on dates using a chosen date field. Show a Task Calendar whose first displayed day overlaps the final part of a Task’s default one-hour duration, while the Task starts before that day. The overlapping Task is excluded rather than displayed.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty’s Calendar view places records on dates using a chosen date field. Day and Week calendar drag handling accepts a toolbar release inside the offscreen full-grid rectangle and persists a calculated early-morning Due Date.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The drag context measures the full 1152-pixel time grid inside the scroll wrapper. When scrolled, that rectangle extends behind the toolbar. The resolver checks the full rectangle without clipping it to the visible viewport, converts the toolbar pointer position into a snapped time, and sends the accepted destination through the record-update hook.
reproductionPaths: Twenty’s Calendar view places records on dates using a chosen date field. Drag a Task in Calendar Day or Week view and release over the toolbar rather than the time grid. The app treats the release as a time-slot drop and saves an unintended early-morning Due Date.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty’s Calendar view places records on dates using a chosen date field. A Task due at 23:59 loads in the calendar but its card is positioned below the clipped hourly grid on its own start day.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The hourly metrics cap the event end at the 1152-pixel grid boundary but retain a minimum 24-pixel card. Rendering adds a 4-pixel top gap, placing a 23:59 card entirely below the day column. That column hides overflow, so the loaded record has no visible card.
reproductionPaths: Twenty’s Calendar view places records on dates using a chosen date field. A Task due at 23:59 loads in the calendar but its card is positioned below the clipped hourly grid on its own start day.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty can narrow a record list with field filters and a Search any field query. Changing the relative-date amount can reopen its input after the first digit, dropping focus and applying a shorter range than the user typed.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Each valid amount change updates the relative filter and resolves a new range. DateTimePicker uses that range as the ReactDatePicker key and renders RelativeDatePickerHeader inside it. A changed key remounts the header/input, losing focus and local draft state before subsequent keystrokes. Sub-day units render the header outside the keyed calendar.
reproductionPaths: Twenty can narrow a record list with field filters and a Search any field query. Type a multi-digit amount into a relative-date filter, such as a range measured in days. After the first digit the input loses focus, so only a shorter range is applied instead of the intended amount.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty can sort board columns alphabetically or let the user order them manually. Start in Alphabetical mode, drag a column header and confirm Remove Alphabetical sorting. The saved result moves different columns from the requested drag and remains wrong after reload; dragging in Manual mode works.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Drag end stores indices from the displayed Alphabetical columns. Confirmation sets group sort to Manual before reorderRecordGroups reads visible group IDs. The stored alphabetical indices are therefore applied to a different Manual-ordered list, and the resulting positions are saved.
reproductionPaths: Twenty’s Kanban board view arranges record cards in columns, often grouped by status or a linked record. Sort board groups Alphabetically, then drag a column header to a new position. The saved move uses a different underlying order, so a different column arrangement is retained.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty can narrow a record list with field filters and a Search any field query. Numeric record filters accept nonnumeric or formatted values as active conditions without validation. Letters can empty Annual Revenue results, while an Amount threshold containing thousands separators is interpreted as a much smaller prefix and includes records below the displayed threshold.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The numeric-filter input and isRecordFilterValueValid accept a nonempty string without validating a complete numeric literal. Query conversion uses parseFloat, which returns NaN for letters and stops at the first comma in a formatted threshold. Displayed filter text can therefore differ from the numeric predicate sent to the server.
reproductionPaths: Twenty can narrow a record list with field filters and a Search any field query. The basic Annual Revenue filter accepts abc as an active numeric condition and empties the table without identifying the invalid value.

Twenty can narrow a record list with field filters and a Search any field query. An Opportunities (sales deals) Amount threshold containing thousands separators is accepted and displayed but returns records below the threshold.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty saved views display records in a chosen layout and retain their configured settings. The saved-view Delete actions immediately remove the view instead of offering the documented confirmation step.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Both user Delete actions invoke useDestroyViewFromCurrentState directly. It closes the picker, switches away from the active deleted view and persists the DestroyView mutation without a confirmation gate.
reproductionPaths: Twenty saved views display records in a chosen layout and retain their configured settings. The saved-view Delete actions immediately remove the view instead of offering the documented confirmation step.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty can divide table rows or board cards into groups based on a field value. In an Account Owner-grouped Company Table with only configured owner groups, select-all reports hundreds more selected than the displayed groups and Count all totals. Ordinary filtered and ungrouped controls report the correct selected count.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Select all sets hasUserSelectedAllRows and selection atoms from loaded grouped record IDs, while context-store bulk selection uses the separate total aggregate. A grouped aggregate/filter mismatch can make the global selection count exceed the actual matching rows.
reproductionPaths: Twenty can divide table rows or board cards into groups based on a field value. In an Account Owner-grouped Company Table with only configured owner groups, select-all reports hundreds more selected than the displayed groups and Count all totals. Ordinary filtered and ungrouped controls report the correct selected count.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty saved views display records in a chosen layout and retain their configured settings. After widening Company Name to about 400px on desktop and scrolling right, narrowing to 390px leaves Name covering the viewport and later-column values and footer. Scrolling fully left and back compacts Name and exposes the values.
logicalBugs.rootCause: RecordTableScrollAndZIndexEffect compacts the first column only inside its scroll-event handler when isMobile is true. Changing the viewport alone does not recompute that flag; RecordTableColumnWidthEffect keeps the saved wide first-column size when the flag is false, so the sticky Name column covers later columns.
reproductionPaths: Twenty saved views display records in a chosen layout and retain their configured settings. On desktop, widen Company Name and scroll the table horizontally, then narrow the window to phone width. The Name column remains so wide that it covers later values and the footer; scrolling left and back makes it compact correctly.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty saved views display records in a chosen layout and retain their configured settings. Pressing Ctrl+A to select an unfiltered large Tasks Table, then pressing it again, clears the initially loaded checkboxes but leaves offscreen rows selected. Scrolling reveals checked rows, while mouse clearing and a small filtered control clear correctly.
logicalBugs.rootCause: useSelectAllRows resets selection when currentAllRowsSelectedStatus is all and clears loaded row flags, then unconditionally sets hasUserSelectedAllRows to true. useLoadRecordsToVirtualRows uses that flag to select subsequently loaded records. The second Ctrl+A therefore clears current checkboxes but re-enables selection for offscreen rows.
reproductionPaths: Twenty saved views display records in a chosen layout and retain their configured settings. In a large unfiltered Tasks Table, press Ctrl+A to select all rows and press it again to clear them. Loaded checkboxes clear but rows reached by scrolling remain selected; mouse clearing and a small filtered list work.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty saved views display records in a chosen layout and retain their configured settings. Opening an owner’s saved unlisted filtered Company view URL as another workspace member retains that viewId in the URL but displays All Companies without its saved filter. A saved Workspace-visible view URL opens with the correct filter; People shows the same fallback variation.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Shared view lookup uses the receiving member's loaded view collection. An unlisted view belonging to another user is absent from that collection; view initialization falls back to another available view without resolving or explicitly rejecting the requested viewId, so URL and active view disagree.
reproductionPaths: Twenty saved views display records in a chosen layout and retain their configured settings. As another workspace member, open a link to an owner’s unlisted saved view with a filter. The URL retains the requested view but the page displays the unfiltered default list; a workspace-visible saved view opens correctly.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty’s Table view has a header checkbox for selecting all records. Select all Company rows, then make one large jump through the partially loaded list. The header changes to partly selected although the selected total is unchanged and visible rows remain checked; gradual scrolling avoids the mismatch. No missing bulk-action targets were demonstrated.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Virtualized row loading assigns IDs at absolute real indexes in a sparse array after a distant scroll jump. The header compares selectedRowIds.filter(...).length, which skips sparse holes, with allRecordIds.length, which includes the unfilled index range. Even though newly fetched records inherit select-all, this sparse-array length mismatch reports partial selection.
reproductionPaths: Twenty’s Table view has a header checkbox for selecting all records. Select all Company rows, then make one large jump through the partially loaded list. The header changes to partly selected although the selected total is unchanged and visible rows remain checked; gradual scrolling avoids the mismatch. No missing bulk-action targets were demonstrated.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty’s Calendar view places records on dates using a chosen date field. Creating a view from a saved Calendar configuration uses Month instead of the source Week or Day period. The copied period persists while the source configuration remains intact.
logicalBugs.rootCause: useCreateViewFromCurrentView always sets calendarLayout to MONTH for a new Calendar view, including create-from-current. It does not copy the current saved calendar period/layout.
reproductionPaths: Twenty’s Calendar view places records on dates using a chosen date field. Creating a view from a saved Calendar configuration uses Month instead of the source Week or Day period. The copied period persists while the source configuration remains intact.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty saved views display records in a chosen layout and retain their configured settings. Opening a newly added Date filter at 390px clips the calendar’s Saturday column and next-month arrow. Desktop and reopening the same popup expose those controls; horizontal scrolling does not recover the clipped edge in the fresh popup.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The filter dropdown uses the generic overlay positioning/overflow container for a full date-picker panel without a viewport-width constraint at the fresh mobile breakpoint. The panel can extend beyond the clipped viewport, making its controls unreachable.
reproductionPaths: Twenty saved views display records in a chosen layout and retain their configured settings. Open a newly added Date filter at phone width. The calendar popup clips Saturday and the next-month arrow, and horizontal scrolling does not recover them; desktop or reopening the popup exposes them.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty’s Kanban board view arranges record cards in columns, often grouped by status or a linked record. Returning through a record breadcrumb (page navigation link) reopens the Kanban board at the top-left, losing its previous browsing position.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The Kanban migration uses native board scrolling but does not retain and restore its horizontal and vertical positions across record-page unmount/remount. Initial board query resets scroll, while the generic restoration hook is not mounted for that board scroll owner.
reproductionPaths: Twenty’s Kanban board view arranges record cards in columns, often grouped by status or a linked record. Scroll a Kanban board, open one of its records and use the record breadcrumb (page navigation link) to return. The board reopens at the top-left instead of the previous browsing position.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty’s Kanban board view arranges record cards in columns, often grouped by status or a linked record. Changing grouping or layout on a built-in saved view can revert its effective grouping and leave a blank Table, Kanban (a board of cards in columns) or Calendar despite a nonzero record count. In By Stage, adding a Company group can switch the field back to Stage while retaining incompatible groups; newly created custom views work.
logicalBugs.rootCause: MetadataEventPublisher routes view events through the generic overridable-entity sanitizer, but resolveOverridableEntityEventBatchOverrides does not include view in its supported entities. The event therefore pushes base built-in view properties instead of effective saved overrides. Frontend metadata then replaces the effective layout/grouping with base values while associated group configuration remains changed.
reproductionPaths: Twenty’s Kanban board view arranges record cards in columns, often grouped by status or a linked record. On the built-in Opportunities (sales deals) By Stage board, change Group by to Company and add a Company through New group. Grouping switches back to Stage while the new group configuration remains, leaving a blank board.

Twenty’s Kanban board view arranges record cards in columns, often grouped by status or a linked record. Existing Tasks By Status and Opportunities (sales deals) By Stage views become blank after changing their layout/grouping. The views retain record counts and settings but lose all visible records and groups after reload. Newly created custom views render successfully.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty’s Kanban board view arranges record cards in columns, often grouped by status or a linked record. The existing Opportunities (sales deals) → By Stage saved board shows a record count of 150 but renders an empty board after reload. Switching Group by from Stage to Owner and back to Stage restores populated columns only until the next reload. Reproduced after a fresh sign-in; a newly created board did not reproduce this failure.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Standard view updates compute group-recreation side effects by comparing the stored base view to a view with overrides resolved. When the effective grouping differs from its base field, unrelated later updates can delete/recreate groups against inconsistent grouping metadata; missing view override resolution in pushed events compounds the mismatch.
reproductionPaths: Twenty’s Kanban board view arranges record cards in columns, often grouped by status or a linked record. Reload the existing Opportunities (sales deals) By Stage board. It reports records but shows no cards; switching grouping away from Stage and back temporarily restores them, while a newly created board does not show this failure.

logicalBugs.description: Twenty’s Calendar view places records on dates using a chosen date field. Calendar cards expose working checkboxes but their selected state is not reflected in the list header, unlike Table and Kanban (a board of cards in columns).
logicalBugs.rootCause: Calendar selection derives selected IDs through recordIndexAllRecordIdsComponentSelector, which reads board/table per-group ID state. Calendar loading writes recordCalendarRecordIdsComponentState instead, so checked calendar cards do not enter the command-context selected-ID list.
reproductionPaths: Twenty’s Calendar view places records on dates using a chosen date field. Click a record checkbox on a Calendar card. The checkbox works, but the list header does not reflect the selected-record state as it does for Table and Kanban (a board of cards in columns).

logicalBugs.description: Twenty’s Kanban board view arranges record cards in columns, often grouped by status or a linked record. Saving a filtered Opportunities (sales deals) table as a new Kanban view fails with a missing main-group field error although Stage is shown as selected. Creating a Kanban through Add view works.
logicalBugs.rootCause: create-from-current uses sourceView.mainGroupByFieldMetadataId instead of the picker's new Kanban grouping. Converting an ungrouped Table therefore sends null grouping even while the form displays Stage; creation fails, and the picker does not restore its persisting flag on that failure path.
reproductionPaths: Twenty’s Kanban board view arranges record cards in columns, often grouped by status or a linked record. Save a filtered Opportunities (sales deals) Table as a new Kanban view. Creation fails for a missing main grouping field despite Stage appearing selected; creating a board through Add view works.
